item.title: Oleshky evacuees reunite with families after truce allows crossing back into Ukraine
item.description:
The US upped the pressure on its ostensible allies as part of its push for a truce in the Russia-Ukraine war. Kyiv has paused its strikes on Russian refineries at the behest of Washington, which is trying to corral runaway fuel prices, The Wall Street Journal reported, while Reuters said the Pentagon had urged European leaders to calm their rhetoric over the threat of Russian aggression. The moves come as Russia’s foreign minister entered the US to attend a meeting of G20 foreign ministers, and after the Trump administration waived new sanctions on Russian energy and reached a diesel deal with the Kremlin — decisions met with unease in Europe , which sees Washington as unnecessarily pressuring Kyiv. — Prashant Rao

item.title: Tusk defends overhaul of Poland’s constitutional court despite protests
item.description:
Prime minister says shake-up is vital to restore tribunal crippled by years of political disputes Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, has vowed to see through a contested overhaul of the country’s constitutional court, declaring that “in certain matters, there can be no compromise”. In a prime-time television address on Saturday night , Tusk was defiant, despite overnight protests that saw riot police drafted to protect the court’s building, saying the shake-up was vital to restore a tribunal crippled by years of political disputes. item.title: Some 320,000 demonstrators take part in largely peaceful protests across France
item.description:
Thousands of rioters swarmed the streets of Paris again on Saturday, launching Molotov cocktails at police officers — while protesters in Lyon burned American and Israeli flags. According to a report from French newspaper Le Monde , some 320,000 protesters gathered on the outskirts of Paris for a march that was, at the outset, relatively peaceful. Some of the protesters wore Halloween costumes as they marched — and after several weeks of unrest, police were out in force to make sure that things stayed under control. item.title: Election officials worry about DOJ monitoring of Tuesday's vote
item.description:
Order says local officials can’t be forced to separate or stop counting ballots that the government deems to be disputed A federal judge has barred the justice department from threatening or coercing election workers to stop processing ballots. The temporary restraining order issued by the US district judge Trina Thompson in the northern district of California late Friday also bars the justice department from demanding local election officials segregate or not count ballots that the federal government deems may have been illegally cast by immigrants, something that is exceedingly rare. item.title: ICE agent charged for hitting Texas immigrant with vehicle during pursuit
item.description:
A Texas grand jury indicted ICE officer Mario Alberto Morales with a charge of second-degree aggravated assault Friday after prosecutors said he deliberately drove his SUV into a fleeing immigrant in early October. Why it matters: This may be the first time an ICE agent has ever been indicted in Texas, making it a rare case of a federal immigration officer facing state charges. What they're saying: Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare announced the grand jury's charge of second-degree aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, namely a motor vehicle. Morales faces two to 20 years if convicted, Teare said. "Just because you have an ICE badge or any badge, if you are in Harris County and you are violating our community members' constitutional rights, there will be repercussions," he said. Catch up quick: Morales struck Miguel Parra Hernandez on Oct. 10 as Parra Hernandez fled on foot.…
